verses.sanskrit:
दुर्योधन उवाच।
              दायं तु विविधं तस्मै शृणु मे गदतोऽनघ। यज्ञार्थं राजभिर्दतं महान्तं धनसञ्चयम्॥१॥
verses.english: Duryodhana said O sinless one, listen to me as I describe that large mass of wealth, consisting of various kinds of tributes presented to him (Yudhishthira) by the kings of the earth.

verses.sanskrit: मेरुमन्दरयोर्मध्ये शैलोदामभितो नदीम्। ये ते कीचकवेणूनां छायां रम्यामुपासते॥२॥
verses.english: Those, that live on the banks of the river Shailoda flowing between the mountains Meru and Mandara and enjoy the delicious shade of the groves of Kichaka bamboo,
verses.bhavadeepa: दायं करार्थं देयं धनं ‘दायो दाने यौतकादिधने’ इति विश्वः ॥१॥

verses.sanskrit: खषा एकासनाद्यर्हाः प्रदरा दीर्घवेणवः। पारदाश्च कुलिन्दाश्च तङ्कणाः परतङ्कणाः॥३॥
verses.english: Namely (the kings) of the khasas, the Ekasanas, the Arhas, the Pradaras, the Dirghavenus, the Paradas, the Kulindas, the Tanganas, and the other Tanganas,

verses.sanskrit: तद्वै पिपीलिकं नाम उद्धृतं यत्पिपीलिकैः। जातरूपं द्रोणमेयमहार्षुः पुञ्जशो नृपाः॥४॥
verses.english: Brought as tribute heaps of gold measured in Dronas (jars) and raised from underneath the earth by ants, and therefore called after the ants.

verses.sanskrit: कृष्णाঁल्ललामांश्चमरान्शुक्लांश्चान्यान्शशिप्रभान्। हिमवत्पुष्पजं चैव स्वादुक्षौद्र तथा बहु॥५॥
verses.english: The powerful mountain tribes, having brought as tribute many soft and black Chamaras and many others as white as the moon-beam, and also sweet honey extracted from the flowers growing on the Himalayas and also from the Mechelia champaka, and also garlands of flowers brought from the land of the northern Kurus, and also various kinds of plants from the north, even from the Kailasa (mountain), waited at the gate with their heads down, being refused admittance.

verses.sanskrit: उत्तरेभ्यः कुरुभ्यश्चाप्यपोढं माल्यमम्बुभिः। उत्तरादपि कैलासादोषधीः सुमहाबलाः॥६॥
पार्वतीया बलिं चान्यमाहृत्य प्रणताः स्थिताः। अजातशत्रोनृपतेर्द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः॥७॥
ये परार्धे हिमवतः सूर्योदयगिरौ नृपाः। कारूषे च समुद्रान्ते लौहित्यमभितश्च ये॥८॥
verses.english: O lord, I also saw many Kirata kings, armed with cruel weapons and ever engaged in cruel deeds, living on fruits and roots and wearing skins, who live on the slopes of the Himalayas and the mountain from behind which the sun rises and in the Karusha country on the sea coast and on the both sides of the Lohitya mountain.

verses.sanskrit: फलमूलाशना ये च किराताश्चर्मवाससः। क्रूरशस्त्राः क्रूरकृतस्तांश्च पश्याम्यहं प्रभो॥९॥
चन्दनागरुकाष्ठानां भारान्कालीयकस्य च। चर्मरत्नसुवर्णानि गन्धानां चैव राशयः॥१०॥
verses.english: O king, having brought loads of Chandana and alone and also black aloes and heaps of valuable skins and much wealth and perfumes, and also ten thousand serving maids of the Kirata race, and many beautiful birds and animals of remote countries.

verses.sanskrit: कैरातकीनामयुतं दासीनां च विशंपते। आहृत्य रमणीयार्थान्दूरगान्मृगपक्षिणः॥११॥
निचितं पर्वतेभ्यश्च हिरण्यं भूरिवर्चसम्। बलिं च कृत्स्त्रमादाय द्वारि तिष्टन्ति वारिताः॥१२॥
verses.english: And also much gold of great splendour procured from the mountains, waited at the gate, being refused admittance.

verses.sanskrit: कैराता दरदा दर्वाः शूरा वै यमकास्तथा। औदुम्बरा दुर्विभागा पारदा बाल्हिकैः सह॥१३॥
verses.english: The Kiratas, the Daradas, the Darvas, the Shiras, the Vaiamakas, the Audumbaras, the Durvibhagas, the Paradas the Valhikas.
verses.bhavadeepa: निचितं राशीकृतं पर्वतेभ्योऽपि भूरिं वर्चसं तेजस्वि अर्शआद्यच् ॥१२॥

verses.sanskrit: काश्मीराश्च कुमाराश्च घोरका हंसकास्तथा। शिबित्रिगर्तयौधेया राजन्या भद्रकेकयाः॥१४॥
verses.english: The Kashmiras, the Kumaras, the Ghorakas, the Hansakayanas, the Shibis the Trigartas, the Yaudheyas, the rulers of the Madras, the Kaikeyas,

verses.sanskrit: अम्बष्ठाः कौकुरास्तार्क्ष्या वस्त्रपाः पल्हवैः सह। वशातलाश्च मौलेयाः सह क्षुद्रकमालवैः॥१५॥
verses.english: The Ambashthas, the Kaukuras, the Tarkshyas, the Vastrapas, with the Pahlvas the Vashatalas, the Mauleyas, the Kshudrakas, the Malavas,

verses.sanskrit: पौण्ड्रिकाः कुकुराश्चैव शकाश्चैव विशांपते। अङ्गावङ्गाश्च पुण्ड्राश्च शाणवत्या गयास्तथा॥१६॥
verses.english: O king, the Paundrayas, the Kukkuras, the Shakas, the Angas, the Vangas, the Pundras, the Shanavatyas and the Gayas,

verses.sanskrit: सुजातयः श्रेणिमन्तः श्रेयांसः शस्त्रधारिणः। अहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशोऽजातशत्रवे॥१७॥
verses.english: These well-born, greatly fortunate excellent and well-skilled in arms Kshatriyas brought tribute by hundreds and thousands.

verses.sanskrit: वङ्काः कलिङ्गा मगधास्ताम्रलिप्ताः सपुण्ड्रकाः। दौवालिकाः सागरकाः पत्रोर्णाः शैशवास्तथा॥१८॥
verses.english: The Vangas, the Kalingas, the Magadhas, the Tamraliptas, the Sapundrakas the Dauvalikas, the Sagarakas, the Patrornas, the Shaishavas,

verses.sanskrit: तत्रस्था द्वारपालैस्ते बहवस्तत्र भारत। कृतकालाः सुवलयस्ततो द्वारमवाप्स्यथ॥१९॥
verses.english: O descendant of Bharata, innumerable Karnapravaranas who came to the gate were told by the gate-keepers at the command of the king (Yudhishthira) that if they could wait and bring good tribute, they would (then) get admittance.

verses.sanskrit: ईषादन्तान्हेमकक्ष्यान्पद्मवर्णान्कुथा वृतान्। शैलाभान्नित्यमत्तांश्चाप्यभितः काम्यकं सरः॥२०॥
verses.english: They (therefore) each gave one thousand elephants with tusks like the shafts of plough and girdles made of gold and with coverlets of fine blankets of the colour of lotus. They were darkish like rocks and they were always rusty, they were all procured from the banks of the Kamyaka lake and they were covered with defensive armour. They were also very patient and they were all of the best breed. Having made these presents, the kings were admitted (into the sacrificial ground).
verses.bhavadeepa: कृतकालाः कृतप्रस्तावाः कृतद्वारा इति पाठे द्वारं प्रतीहारेण सख्यम् ॥१९॥

verses.sanskrit: दत्वैकैको दशशतान्कुञ्जरान्कवचावृतान्। क्षमावतः कुलीनाश्च द्वारेण प्राविशंस्तथा॥२१॥
एते चान्ये च बहवो गणा दिगभ्यः समागताः। अन्यैश्चोपाहृतान्यत्र रत्नानीह महात्मभिः॥२२॥
verses.english: These and many other (kings), coming from various regions, and also others who brought a great mass of gems and jewels, all assembled there.

verses.sanskrit: राजा चित्ररथो नाम गन्धर्वो वासवानुगः। शतानि चत्वार्यददद्धयानां वातरंहसाम्॥२३॥
verses.english: The king, named Chitraratha, the friend of Indra, gave five hundred horses with the spread of wind.

verses.sanskrit: तुम्बुरुस्तु प्रमुदितो गन्धर्वो वाजिनां शतम्। आम्रपत्रसवर्णानामददद्धेममालिनाम्॥२४॥
verses.english: The Gandharva Tumburu cheerfully gave one hundred horses of the colour of the mango leaf, all adorned with gold (ornaments).

verses.sanskrit: कृती राजा च कौरव्य शूकराणां विशाम्पते। अददद्गजरत्नानां शतानि सुबहून्यथ॥२५॥
verses.english: O king, O descendant of Kuru, the renowned king of the Shukaras gave many hundreds of valuable elephants.

verses.sanskrit: विराटेन तु मत्स्येन बल्यर्थं हेममालिनाम्। कुञ्जराणां सहस्रे द्वे मत्तानां समुपाहृते॥२६॥
verses.english: The king of Matsya, Virata, gave as tribute two thousand elephants adorned with gold (ornaments).

verses.sanskrit: जवसत्वोपपन्नानां वयस्थानां नराधिप। बलिं च कृत्स्नमादाय पाण्डवेभ्यो न्यवेदयत्॥२८॥
verses.english: O king, they were all endued with speed and strength and they were all in the full vigour of their youth. These and many other wealth he offered to the Pandavas.

verses.sanskrit: पांशुराष्ट्राद्वसुदानो राजा षड्विंशतिं गजान्। अश्वानां चसहस्रे द्वे राजन्काञ्चनमालिनाम्॥२९॥
verses.english: O monarch, king Vasudana from the kingdom of Pánshu gave twenty six elephants and two thousand horses all adorned with gold (ornaments).

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञसेनेन दासीनां सहस्राणि चतुर्दश। दासानामयुतं चैव सदाराणां विशाम्पते। गजयुक्ता महाराज रथाः षड्विंशतिस्तथा॥२९॥
verses.english: O monarch, king Vasudana from the kingdom of Pánshu gave twenty six elephants and two thousand horses all adorned with gold (ornaments).

verses.sanskrit: राज्यं च कृत्स्नं पार्थेभ्यो यज्ञार्थं वै निवेदितम्। वासुदेवोऽपि वार्ष्णेयो मानं कुर्वन्किरीटिनः॥३०॥
verses.english: O king, Yajnasena presented to the sons of Pritha for their sacrifice fourteen thousand serving maids and ten thousands serving men with their wives. O great king, also many hundreds of excellent elephants, twenty six cars with elephants yoked to them and also his whole kingdom. Vasudeva of the Vrishni race (Krishna) in order to increase the dignity of Kiriti Arjuna.

verses.sanskrit: अददद्गजमुख्यानां सहस्राणि चतुर्दश। आत्मा हि कृष्णः पार्थस्य कृष्णस्यात्मा धनञ्जयः॥३१॥
verses.english: Gave fourteen thousand excellent elephants. Krishna is the soul of Partha (Arjuna), and Dhananjaya (Arjuna) is the soul of Krishna.

verses.sanskrit: यद्ब्रूयादर्जुनः कृष्णं सर्वं कुर्यादसंशयम्। कृष्णो धनञ्जयस्यार्थे स्वर्गलोकमपि त्यजेत्॥३२॥
verses.english: Whatever Arjuna may say Krishna is certain to accomplish. Krishna can abandon heaven itself for the sake of Dhananjaya (Arjuna).

verses.sanskrit: तथैव पार्थः कृष्णार्थे प्राणानपि परित्यजेत्। सुरभींश्चन्दनरसान्हेमकुम्भसमास्थितान्॥३३॥
verses.english: Partha also can sacrifice his life for the sake of Krishna. Though, numberless golden jars filled with fragrant Chandana.

verses.sanskrit: मलयाद्दर्दुराच्चैव चन्दनागुरुसञ्चयान्। मणिरत्नानि भास्वन्ति काञ्चनं सूक्ष्मवस्त्रकम्॥३४॥
verses.english: From the Malaya hills and loads of sandals and alone woods from the Daraduras hills, many very costly gems and many fine cloths inlaid with gold.

verses.sanskrit: चोलपाण्ड्यावपि द्वारं न लेभाते ह्युपस्थितौ। समुद्रसारं वैदूर्यं मुक्तासङ्घांस्तथैव च॥३५॥
verses.english: Were brought by the kings of Chola and Pandya yet they could not get admittance. That best of sea-born gems, Vaidurya and heap of pearls.

verses.sanskrit: शतशश्च कुथांस्तत्र सिंहलाः समुपाहरन्। संवृता मणिचीरैस्तु श्यामास्ताम्रान्तलोचनाः॥३६॥
verses.english: And hundreds of coverlets for elephants were presented by the kings of the Singhalas. Innumerable dark-coloured men with copper coloured eyes, attired with robes adorned with gems.

verses.sanskrit: ता गृहीत्वा नरास्तत्र द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः। प्रीत्यर्थं ब्राह्मणश्चैव क्षत्रियाश्च विनिर्जिताः॥३७॥
verses.english: Waited at the gate with their presents being refused admittance. In order to gratify (Yudhishthira) many Brahmanas and many Kshatriyas who have been vanquished, Vaishyas and serving Shudras brought tribute from the love and respect of Yudhishthira even all the Mlecchas came to his palace. Men of all orders, good, indifferent and low belonging to various tribes came from various regions.

verses.sanskrit: उपाजह्रुर्विशश्चैव शूद्राः शुश्रूषवस्तथा। प्रीत्या च बहुमानाच्चाप्युपागच्छन्युधिष्ठिरम्॥३८॥
सर्वे म्लेच्छाः सर्ववर्णा आदिमध्यान्तजास्तथा। नानादेशसमुत्थैश्च नानाजातिभिरेव च॥३९॥
पर्यस्त इव लोकोऽयं युधिष्ठिरनिवेशने। उच्चावचानुपग्राहान्राजभिः प्रापितान्बहून्॥४०॥
verses.english: And made the palace of Yudhishthira an epitom of all the world. seeing the king offer such excellent and valuable presents, I wish for death from grief. O king, I shall now tell you about the servants of the Pandavas,

verses.sanskrit: शत्रूणां पश्यतो दुःखान्मुमूर्षा मे व्यजायत। भृत्यास्तु ये पाण्डवानां तांस्ते वक्ष्यामि पार्थिव॥४१॥
verses.bhavadeepa: पर्यस्त इव भूदेशोऽपि स्वर्गीभूत इव उपग्राहानुपहारान् ॥४०॥

verses.sanskrit: येषामामं च पक्वं च संविधत्ते युधिष्ठिरः। अयुतं त्रीणि पद्मानि गजारोहाः ससादिनः॥४२॥
verses.english: To whom Yudhishthira supplies both cooked and uncooked food. There are hundred thousand billions of soldiers mounted on elephants, and also horsemen.

verses.sanskrit: रथानामर्बुदं चापि पादाता बहवस्तथा। प्रमीयमाणमामं च पच्यमानं तथैव च॥४३॥
verses.english: And also a hundred million of cars and numberless foot-soldiers. At one place raw food grains are being measured out and at another they all being cooked.

verses.sanskrit: विसृज्यमानं चान्यत्र पुण्याहस्वन एव च। नाभुक्तवन्तं नापीतं नालङ्कृतमसत्कृतम्॥४४॥
verses.english: At another place they are distributed; the sound of festivity is heard every where. I have not seen a single man amongst the four orders who had not got in Yudhishthira's palace food, drink, ornament and reception. Eighty eight thousand Snatakas leading domestic life.
verses.bhavadeepa: प्रमीयमाणं खार्यादिना मानेन गण्यमानम् आमम् अपक्वम् ॥४३॥

verses.sanskrit: अपश्यं सर्ववर्णानां युधिष्ठिरनिवेशने। अष्टाशीति सहस्राणि स्नातका गृहमेधिनः॥४५॥
त्रिंशद्दासीक एकैको यान्बिभर्ति युधिष्ठिरः। सुप्रीताः परितुष्टाश्च ते ह्याशंसन्त्यरिक्षयम्॥४६॥
verses.english: Were all supported by Yudhishthira who presented each with thirty serving girls. They being thus gratified always pray for the destruction of his foe.

verses.sanskrit: दशान्यानि सहस्राणि यतीनामूर्ध्वरेतसाम्। भुञ्जते रुक्मपात्रीभिर्युधिष्ठिरनिवेशने॥४७॥
verses.english: Ten thousand Ascetics with their passions under complete control daily cat in golden plates in Yudhishthira's palace.

verses.sanskrit: अभुक्तं भुक्तवद्वापि सर्वमाकुब्जवामनम्। अभुञ्जाना याज्ञसेनी प्रत्यवैक्षद्विशाम्पते॥४८॥
verses.english: O king, Yajnaseni (Draupadi) without herself taking any food, daily sees whether everybody, including even the dwarfs and the deformed has eaten.

verses.sanskrit: द्वौ करौ न प्रयच्छेतां कुन्तीपुत्राय भारत। साम्बन्धिकेन पाञ्चालाः सख्येनान्धकवृष्णयः॥४९॥
verses.english: O descendant of Bharata, only two (race) do not pay tribute to the son of Kunti, the Panchalas on account of their relationship by marriage and the Andhakas and the Vrishnis on account of their friendship (with the Pandavas).
